Workshop 1: Mapping Philippine Cities

  • Show All Code
  • Hide All Code
  • View Source

Land Rent Gradients and Urban Productivity in Metro Manila

Author

Jem Marie Nario

Overview

This workshop introduces spatial data analysis in R using real Philippine Statistical Authority (PSA) data. By the end of this session, you will be able to:

  1. Load and inspect a city-level spatial dataset for Metro Manila (NCR)
  2. Join tabular data to shapefiles using sf
  3. Produce choropleth maps with ggplot2
  4. Visualize the land rent gradient — how rent declines with distance from the central business district (CBD)
  5. Map human capital indicators as proxies for urban productivity
Note

Data sources
- FIES 2023 (Family Income and Expenditure Survey) — PSA
- CPH 2020 (Census of Population and Housing, Form 2) — PSA
- Both datasets are aggregated to the city/municipality level (n = 17 NCR LGUs)

1 · Setup

1.1 Install and load packages

Code 
# Install if needed (run once)
# install.packages(c("sf", "ggplot2", "dplyr", "ggrepel",
#                    "scales", "viridis", "patchwork", "geodata"))

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)          # spatial data structures
library(geodata)     # get spatial data polygons
library(ggplot2)     # grammar of graphics
library(ggrepel)     # non-overlapping labels
library(dplyr)       # data wrangling
library(scales)      # axis formatting
library(viridis)     # colour scales
library(patchwork)   # combine plots

1.3 Variable reference

Variable Source Description
city — City/municipality name
lat, lon — City centroid (WGS84)
dist_cbd_km — Distance from Makati CBD (km)
mean_rentval FIES 2023 Mean rent value PHP/year (actual + imputed)
mean_actrent FIES 2023 Mean actual rent paid by renters
mean_inc FIES 2023 Mean total household income PHP/year
rent_inc_ratio FIES 2023 Rent-to-income ratio
wage_inc_share FIES 2023 Wage share of total income
mean_educ_exp FIES 2023 Mean education expenditure PHP/year
pct_renters_fies FIES 2023 % households paying actual rent
n_hh CPH 2020 Total housing units
pct_renter CPH 2020 % renting house and lot (H1=4)
pct_any_rent CPH 2020 % with any rent burden
pct_makeshift_wall CPH 2020 % with makeshift outer walls
pct_strong_wall CPH 2020 % with concrete/brick walls
pct_college_grad CPH 2020 % adults 25+ with college degree
pct_some_college CPH 2020 % adults 25+ with any college
pct_literate CPH 2020 % literate population
pct_ofw CPH 2020 % overseas workers

2 · Introduction to Spatial Data

2.1 What is spatial data?

Spatial data attaches location to observations. In urban and regional economics, this means we can ask not just what a city’s rent level is, but where it sits relative to other cities, economic centres, and infrastructure.

The key R package for spatial data is sf (simple features). It stores geographic data as a standard data frame with an extra geometry column.

2.2 Get the NCR shapefile

We use the GADM administrative boundaries (level 2 = city/municipality):

Code 
ph_adm2    <- gadm(country = "PHL", level = 2, path = "data/")
ph_adm2_sf <- st_as_sf(ph_adm2)

ncr_sf <- ph_adm2_sf %>%
  filter(NAME_1 == "Metropolitan Manila") %>%
  mutate(city = case_when(
    NAME_2 == "Las Piñas"     ~ "Las Pinas",
    NAME_2 == "Parañaque"     ~ "Paranaque",
    NAME_2 == "Kalookan City" ~ "Caloocan",
    NAME_2 == "Makati City"   ~ "Makati",
    NAME_2 == "Pasay City"    ~ "Pasay",
    NAME_2 == "Pasig City"    ~ "Pasig",
    TRUE                      ~ NAME_2
  ))

cat("NCR cities in shapefile:", nrow(ncr_sf), "\n")
NCR cities in shapefile: 17

2.3 Join tabular data to shapefile

Code 
ncr_map <- ncr_sf %>%
  left_join(ncr_city, by = "city")

cat("Unmatched:", sum(is.na(ncr_map$mean_rentval)), "\n")
Unmatched: 0
Code 
# City centroids for all label layers
ncr_centroids <- ncr_map %>%
  st_centroid() %>%
  mutate(
    lon = st_coordinates(.)[, 1],
    lat = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]
  )

plot(st_geometry(ncr_map), main = "NCR Cities — Geometry Check")
Tip

Key concept: the join key
The left_join(by = "city") links rows in the shapefile to rows in our dataset using the city name as the common key. In production, it is better to use a numeric code (PSGC) to avoid string-matching errors — but city names work fine for our 17-unit NCR dataset.

3 · Choropleth Maps

A choropleth map shades geographic units by a variable’s value. We use ggplot2 for publication-quality static maps.

3.1 Mean rent value

Code 
ggplot(ncr_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = mean_rentval), color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data          = ncr_centroids,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = city),
    size          = 3,
    color         = "grey20",
    max.overlaps  = 20,
    segment.size  = 0.3,
    segment.color = "grey60"
  ) +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    palette   = "YlOrRd",
    direction = 1,
    labels    = comma_format(prefix = "₱"),
    name      = "Mean Rent\n(PHP/year)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title   = "Land Rent Value — NCR Cities",
    caption = "Source: FIES 2023 (PSA)"
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5,
                                   margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.caption    = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 8),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

3.2 College graduation rate

Code 
ggplot(ncr_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pct_college_grad), color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = ncr_centroids,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = city),
    size = 3, color = "grey20",
    max.overlaps = 20,
    segment.size = 0.3, segment.color = "grey60"
  ) +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    palette = "Blues", direction = 1,
    labels  = function(x) paste0(round(x, 1), "%"),
    name    = "College Grads\n(% adults 25+)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title   = "Human Capital — College Graduation Rate",
    caption = "Source: CPH 2020 (PSA)"
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5,
                                   margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.caption    = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 8),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

3.3 Side-by-side comparison

Code 
p_rent <- ggplot(ncr_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = mean_rentval), color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = ncr_centroids,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = city),
    size = 2.5, color = "grey20", max.overlaps = 20,
    segment.size = 0.3, segment.color = "grey60"
  ) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "YlOrRd", direction = 1,
                       labels = comma_format(prefix = "₱"),
                       name = "Rent (PHP/yr)") +
  labs(title = "Land Rent", caption = "FIES 2023") +
  theme_void(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

p_college <- ggplot(ncr_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pct_college_grad), color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = ncr_centroids,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = city),
    size = 2.5, color = "grey20", max.overlaps = 20,
    segment.size = 0.3, segment.color = "grey60"
  ) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Blues", direction = 1,
                       labels = function(x) paste0(round(x, 1), "%"),
                       name = "College (%)") +
  labs(title = "Human Capital", caption = "CPH 2020") +
  theme_void(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

p_rent + p_college
Note

What do you notice?
The two maps should show a broadly similar spatial pattern — cities with higher rent tend to have higher college graduation rates. This is the agglomeration premium: skilled workers cluster where productivity (and land rent) is highest.

4 · The Land Rent Gradient

The Alonso–Muth–Mills (AMM) model predicts that land rent declines with distance from the CBD as households trade off commuting costs against housing costs. Let’s test this with our NCR data.

4.1 Scatter plot: rent vs distance

Code 
ggplot(ncr_city, aes(x = dist_cbd_km, y = mean_rentval)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE,
              colour = "#c0392b", fill = "#fadbd8", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n_hh), colour = "#2c3e50", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = city), size = 3.2, colour = "grey30",
                  max.overlaps = 20) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format(prefix = "₱")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 20, 5)) +
  scale_size_continuous(labels = comma, name = "Housing units") +
  labs(
    title    = "Land Rent Gradient — Metro Manila",
    subtitle = "Mean household rent value vs distance from Makati CBD",
    x        = "Distance from Makati CBD (km)",
    y        = "Mean rent value (PHP/year)",
    caption  = "Sources: FIES 2023, CPH 2020 (PSA)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

4.2 Fit the gradient model

Code 
# Simple log-linear rent gradient model
# ln(rent) = α + β × distance + ε
# β < 0 confirms the AMM prediction

model <- lm(log(mean_rentval) ~ dist_cbd_km, data = ncr_city)
summary(model)

Call:
lm(formula = log(mean_rentval) ~ dist_cbd_km, data = ncr_city)

Residuals:
     Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max 
-0.36798 -0.24709 -0.01114  0.11692  0.52526 

Coefficients:
            Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept) 11.60758    0.14712  78.898  < 2e-16 ***
dist_cbd_km -0.04643    0.01395  -3.327  0.00459 ** 
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Residual standard error: 0.295 on 15 degrees of freedom
Multiple R-squared:  0.4247,    Adjusted R-squared:  0.3863 
F-statistic: 11.07 on 1 and 15 DF,  p-value: 0.004594
Important

Interpreting β
The coefficient on dist_cbd_km tells us: for each additional kilometre from Makati CBD, rent changes by approximately exp(β) - 1 × 100 percent. A negative β confirms the AMM gradient.

4.3 Rent-to-income ratio gradient

Code 
ggplot(ncr_city, aes(x = dist_cbd_km, y = rent_inc_ratio)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE,
              colour = "#8e44ad", fill = "#e8daef", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(colour = "#2c3e50", size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = city), size = 3.2, colour = "grey30",
                  max.overlaps = 20) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 20, 5)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Rent Burden Gradient — Metro Manila",
    subtitle = "Rent-to-income ratio vs distance from Makati CBD",
    x        = "Distance from Makati CBD (km)",
    y        = "Rent-to-income ratio",
    caption  = "Source: FIES 2023 (PSA)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

5 · Human Capital and Urban Productivity

5.1 College graduation vs rent

The human capital theory of cities (Glaeser et al.) argues that skilled workers are more productive in dense, high-rent areas because of knowledge spillovers and thick labour markets.

Code 
ggplot(ncr_city, aes(x = pct_college_grad, y = mean_rentval)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE,
              colour = "#16a085", fill = "#d1f2eb", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n_hh), colour = "#2c3e50", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = city), size = 3.2, colour = "grey30",
                  max.overlaps = 20) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format(prefix = "₱")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  scale_size_continuous(labels = comma, name = "Housing units") +
  labs(
    title    = "Human Capital and Land Rent — Metro Manila",
    subtitle = "Cities with more college graduates command higher rents",
    x        = "College graduation rate (% adults 25+)",
    y        = "Mean rent value (PHP/year)",
    caption  = "Sources: FIES 2023, CPH 2020 (PSA)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

5.2 Education expenditure vs income

Code 
ggplot(ncr_city, aes(x = mean_inc, y = mean_educ_exp)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE,
              colour = "#e67e22", fill = "#fdebd0", linewidth = 1) +

                  max.overlaps = 20) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma_format(prefix = "₱")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format(prefix = "₱")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Education Investment vs Income — Metro Manila",
    subtitle = "Higher-income cities invest more in education",
    x        = "Mean household income (PHP/year)",
    y        = "Mean education expenditure (PHP/year)",
    caption  = "Source: FIES 2023 (PSA)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

5.3 Four-panel productivity dashboard

Code 
p1 <- ggplot(ncr_city, aes(dist_cbd_km, mean_rentval)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "#c0392b",
              fill = "#fadbd8", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = "#2c3e50", size = 2.5) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = city), size = 2.8, max.overlaps = 15) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format(prefix = "₱")) +
  labs(title = "A. Rent Gradient",
       x = "Distance from CBD (km)", y = "Mean rent (PHP/yr)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

p2 <- ggplot(ncr_city, aes(dist_cbd_km, pct_college_grad)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "#2980b9",
              fill = "#d6eaf8", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = "#2c3e50", size = 2.5) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = city), size = 2.8, max.overlaps = 15) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(title = "B. Human Capital Gradient",
       x = "Distance from CBD (km)", y = "College grads (%)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

p3 <- ggplot(ncr_city, aes(pct_college_grad, mean_rentval)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "#16a085",
              fill = "#d1f2eb", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = "#2c3e50", size = 2.5) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = city), size = 2.8, max.overlaps = 15) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format(prefix = "₱")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(title = "C. Rent vs Human Capital",
       x = "College grads (%)", y = "Mean rent (PHP/yr)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

p4 <- ggplot(ncr_city, aes(wage_inc_share, mean_inc)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "#8e44ad",
              fill = "#e8daef", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = "#2c3e50", size = 2.5) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = city), size = 2.8, max.overlaps = 15) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format(prefix = "₱")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(title = "D. Wage Formality vs Income",
       x = "Wage share of income", y = "Mean income (PHP/yr)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

(p1 + p2) / (p3 + p4) +
  plot_annotation(
    title   = "Urban Productivity Dashboard — Metro Manila",
    subtitle = "FIES 2023 + CPH 2020 | City-level analysis (n = 17)",
    caption  = "Sources: PSA FIES 2023, CPH 2020",
    theme    = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13))
  )

6 · Exercises

Tip

Exercise 1 — Map a new variable
Produce a choropleth map of pct_makeshift_wall (informality proxy). Which cities have the highest rates? Does this align with what you know about NCR urban geography?

Tip

Exercise 2 — Test a different gradient
Fit the log-linear gradient model using pct_college_grad as the dependent variable instead of mean_rentval. Is the human capital gradient steeper or flatter than the rent gradient?

Tip

Exercise 3 — OFW and rent
Plot pct_ofw (overseas workers) against dist_cbd_km. Do peripheral cities have more OFWs? What might this tell us about the relationship between local labour market opportunities and international migration?

7 · Key Takeaways

  • Spatial data in R combines a geometry column with regular data frame columns, enabling seamless joins between tabular and geographic data
  • The land rent gradient in Metro Manila broadly follows the AMM prediction: rent declines with distance from Makati CBD
  • Human capital (college graduation) and rent are positively correlated across NCR cities, consistent with agglomeration theory
  • Anomalies (San Juan’s high rent, Valenzuela’s high rent burden) are as instructive as the general pattern — they invite deeper investigation

## Overview

This workshop introduces **spatial data analysis in R** using real
Philippine Statistical Authority (PSA) data. By the end of this session,
you will be able to:

1.  Load and inspect a city-level spatial dataset for Metro Manila (NCR)
2.  Join tabular data to shapefiles using `sf`
3.  Produce choropleth maps with `ggplot2`
4.  Visualize the **land rent gradient** — how rent declines with
    distance from the central business district (CBD)
5.  Map **human capital indicators** as proxies for urban productivity

::: callout-note
**Data sources**\
- **FIES 2023** (Family Income and Expenditure Survey) — PSA\
- **CPH 2020** (Census of Population and Housing, Form 2) — PSA\
- Both datasets are aggregated to the city/municipality level (n = 17
NCR LGUs)
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1 · Setup

### 1.1 Install and load packages

```{r}
#| label: setup

# Install if needed (run once)
# install.packages(c("sf", "ggplot2", "dplyr", "ggrepel",
#                    "scales", "viridis", "patchwork", "geodata"))

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)          # spatial data structures
library(geodata)     # get spatial data polygons
library(ggplot2)     # grammar of graphics
library(ggrepel)     # non-overlapping labels
library(dplyr)       # data wrangling
library(scales)      # axis formatting
library(viridis)     # colour scales
library(patchwork)   # combine plots
```

### 1.2 Load the training dataset

```{r}
#| label: load-data

# Load the pre-assembled NCR city dataset
# Contains FIES 2023 + CPH 2020 variables at city level
load("data/ncr_city_training.RData")   # loads as 'ncr_city'

# Quick look
glimpse(ncr_city)
```

### 1.3 Variable reference

| Variable             | Source    | Description                                 |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| `city`               | —         | City/municipality name                      |
| `lat`, `lon`         | —         | City centroid (WGS84)                       |
| `dist_cbd_km`        | —         | Distance from Makati CBD (km)               |
| `mean_rentval`       | FIES 2023 | Mean rent value PHP/year (actual + imputed) |
| `mean_actrent`       | FIES 2023 | Mean actual rent paid by renters            |
| `mean_inc`           | FIES 2023 | Mean total household income PHP/year        |
| `rent_inc_ratio`     | FIES 2023 | Rent-to-income ratio                        |
| `wage_inc_share`     | FIES 2023 | Wage share of total income                  |
| `mean_educ_exp`      | FIES 2023 | Mean education expenditure PHP/year         |
| `pct_renters_fies`   | FIES 2023 | \% households paying actual rent            |
| `n_hh`               | CPH 2020  | Total housing units                         |
| `pct_renter`         | CPH 2020  | \% renting house and lot (H1=4)             |
| `pct_any_rent`       | CPH 2020  | \% with any rent burden                     |
| `pct_makeshift_wall` | CPH 2020  | \% with makeshift outer walls               |
| `pct_strong_wall`    | CPH 2020  | \% with concrete/brick walls                |
| `pct_college_grad`   | CPH 2020  | \% adults 25+ with college degree           |
| `pct_some_college`   | CPH 2020  | \% adults 25+ with any college              |
| `pct_literate`       | CPH 2020  | \% literate population                      |
| `pct_ofw`            | CPH 2020  | \% overseas workers                         |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 2 · Introduction to Spatial Data

### 2.1 What is spatial data?

Spatial data attaches **location** to observations. In urban and
regional economics, this means we can ask not just *what* a city's rent
level is, but *where* it sits relative to other cities, economic
centres, and infrastructure.

The key R package for spatial data is `sf` (simple features). It stores
geographic data as a standard data frame with an extra **geometry
column**.

### 2.2 Get the NCR shapefile

We use the GADM administrative boundaries (level 2 = city/municipality):

```{r}
#| label: get-shapefile

ph_adm2    <- gadm(country = "PHL", level = 2, path = "data/")
ph_adm2_sf <- st_as_sf(ph_adm2)

ncr_sf <- ph_adm2_sf %>%
  filter(NAME_1 == "Metropolitan Manila") %>%
  mutate(city = case_when(
    NAME_2 == "Las Piñas"     ~ "Las Pinas",
    NAME_2 == "Parañaque"     ~ "Paranaque",
    NAME_2 == "Kalookan City" ~ "Caloocan",
    NAME_2 == "Makati City"   ~ "Makati",
    NAME_2 == "Pasay City"    ~ "Pasay",
    NAME_2 == "Pasig City"    ~ "Pasig",
    TRUE                      ~ NAME_2
  ))

cat("NCR cities in shapefile:", nrow(ncr_sf), "\n")
```

### 2.3 Join tabular data to shapefile

```{r}
#| label: join-data

ncr_map <- ncr_sf %>%
  left_join(ncr_city, by = "city")

cat("Unmatched:", sum(is.na(ncr_map$mean_rentval)), "\n")

# City centroids for all label layers
ncr_centroids <- ncr_map %>%
  st_centroid() %>%
  mutate(
    lon = st_coordinates(.)[, 1],
    lat = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]
  )

plot(st_geometry(ncr_map), main = "NCR Cities — Geometry Check")
```

::: callout-tip
**Key concept: the join key**\
The `left_join(by = "city")` links rows in the shapefile to rows in our
dataset using the city name as the common key. In production, it is
better to use a numeric code (PSGC) to avoid string-matching errors —
but city names work fine for our 17-unit NCR dataset.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3 · Choropleth Maps

A **choropleth map** shades geographic units by a variable's value. We
use `ggplot2` for publication-quality static maps.

### 3.1 Mean rent value

```{r}
#| label: mean rent
#| fig-cap: "Mean household rent value (PHP/year) by NCR city, FIES 2023"

ggplot(ncr_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = mean_rentval), color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data          = ncr_centroids,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = city),
    size          = 3,
    color         = "grey20",
    max.overlaps  = 20,
    segment.size  = 0.3,
    segment.color = "grey60"
  ) +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    palette   = "YlOrRd",
    direction = 1,
    labels    = comma_format(prefix = "₱"),
    name      = "Mean Rent\n(PHP/year)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title   = "Land Rent Value — NCR Cities",
    caption = "Source: FIES 2023 (PSA)"
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5,
                                   margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.caption    = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 8),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```

### 3.2 College graduation rate

```{r}
#| label: map-college
#| fig-cap: "Share of adults 25+ with college degree (%), CPH 2020"

ggplot(ncr_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pct_college_grad), color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = ncr_centroids,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = city),
    size = 3, color = "grey20",
    max.overlaps = 20,
    segment.size = 0.3, segment.color = "grey60"
  ) +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    palette = "Blues", direction = 1,
    labels  = function(x) paste0(round(x, 1), "%"),
    name    = "College Grads\n(% adults 25+)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title   = "Human Capital — College Graduation Rate",
    caption = "Source: CPH 2020 (PSA)"
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5,
                                   margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.caption    = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 8),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```

### 3.3 Side-by-side comparison

```{r}
#| label: map-side-by-side
#| fig-cap: "Rent value vs college graduation rate — NCR cities"
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5

p_rent <- ggplot(ncr_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = mean_rentval), color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = ncr_centroids,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = city),
    size = 2.5, color = "grey20", max.overlaps = 20,
    segment.size = 0.3, segment.color = "grey60"
  ) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "YlOrRd", direction = 1,
                       labels = comma_format(prefix = "₱"),
                       name = "Rent (PHP/yr)") +
  labs(title = "Land Rent", caption = "FIES 2023") +
  theme_void(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

p_college <- ggplot(ncr_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pct_college_grad), color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = ncr_centroids,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = city),
    size = 2.5, color = "grey20", max.overlaps = 20,
    segment.size = 0.3, segment.color = "grey60"
  ) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Blues", direction = 1,
                       labels = function(x) paste0(round(x, 1), "%"),
                       name = "College (%)") +
  labs(title = "Human Capital", caption = "CPH 2020") +
  theme_void(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

p_rent + p_college
```

::: callout-note
**What do you notice?**\
The two maps should show a broadly similar spatial pattern — cities with
higher rent tend to have higher college graduation rates. This is the
**agglomeration premium**: skilled workers cluster where productivity
(and land rent) is highest.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 4 · The Land Rent Gradient

The **Alonso–Muth–Mills (AMM) model** predicts that land rent declines
with distance from the CBD as households trade off commuting costs
against housing costs. Let's test this with our NCR data.

### 4.1 Scatter plot: rent vs distance

```{r}
#| label: rent-gradient
#| fig-cap: "Land rent gradient — NCR cities, 2023"

ggplot(ncr_city, aes(x = dist_cbd_km, y = mean_rentval)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE,
              colour = "#c0392b", fill = "#fadbd8", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n_hh), colour = "#2c3e50", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = city), size = 3.2, colour = "grey30",
                  max.overlaps = 20) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format(prefix = "₱")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 20, 5)) +
  scale_size_continuous(labels = comma, name = "Housing units") +
  labs(
    title    = "Land Rent Gradient — Metro Manila",
    subtitle = "Mean household rent value vs distance from Makati CBD",
    x        = "Distance from Makati CBD (km)",
    y        = "Mean rent value (PHP/year)",
    caption  = "Sources: FIES 2023, CPH 2020 (PSA)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

### 4.2 Fit the gradient model

```{r}
#| label: gradient-model

# Simple log-linear rent gradient model
# ln(rent) = α + β × distance + ε
# β < 0 confirms the AMM prediction

model <- lm(log(mean_rentval) ~ dist_cbd_km, data = ncr_city)
summary(model)
```

::: callout-important
**Interpreting β**\
The coefficient on `dist_cbd_km` tells us: for each additional kilometre
from Makati CBD, rent changes by approximately `exp(β) - 1` × 100
percent. A negative β confirms the AMM gradient.
:::

### 4.3 Rent-to-income ratio gradient

```{r}
#| label: rent-burden-gradient
#| fig-cap: "Rent burden (rent-to-income ratio) vs distance from CBD"

ggplot(ncr_city, aes(x = dist_cbd_km, y = rent_inc_ratio)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE,
              colour = "#8e44ad", fill = "#e8daef", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(colour = "#2c3e50", size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = city), size = 3.2, colour = "grey30",
                  max.overlaps = 20) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 20, 5)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Rent Burden Gradient — Metro Manila",
    subtitle = "Rent-to-income ratio vs distance from Makati CBD",
    x        = "Distance from Makati CBD (km)",
    y        = "Rent-to-income ratio",
    caption  = "Source: FIES 2023 (PSA)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 5 · Human Capital and Urban Productivity

### 5.1 College graduation vs rent

The **human capital theory of cities** (Glaeser et al.) argues that
skilled workers are more productive in dense, high-rent areas because of
knowledge spillovers and thick labour markets.

```{r}
#| label: hk-rent
#| fig-cap: "College graduation rate vs mean rent value — NCR cities"

ggplot(ncr_city, aes(x = pct_college_grad, y = mean_rentval)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE,
              colour = "#16a085", fill = "#d1f2eb", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n_hh), colour = "#2c3e50", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = city), size = 3.2, colour = "grey30",
                  max.overlaps = 20) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format(prefix = "₱")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  scale_size_continuous(labels = comma, name = "Housing units") +
  labs(
    title    = "Human Capital and Land Rent — Metro Manila",
    subtitle = "Cities with more college graduates command higher rents",
    x        = "College graduation rate (% adults 25+)",
    y        = "Mean rent value (PHP/year)",
    caption  = "Sources: FIES 2023, CPH 2020 (PSA)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

### 5.2 Education expenditure vs income

```{r}
#| label: educ-exp
#| fig-cap: "Education expenditure vs household income — NCR cities"

ggplot(ncr_city, aes(x = mean_inc, y = mean_educ_exp)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE,
              colour = "#e67e22", fill = "#fdebd0", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(colour = "#2c3e50", size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = city), size = 3.2, colour = "grey30",
                  max.overlaps = 20) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma_format(prefix = "₱")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format(prefix = "₱")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Education Investment vs Income — Metro Manila",
    subtitle = "Higher-income cities invest more in education",
    x        = "Mean household income (PHP/year)",
    y        = "Mean education expenditure (PHP/year)",
    caption  = "Source: FIES 2023 (PSA)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

### 5.3 Four-panel productivity dashboard

```{r}
#| label: dashboard
#| fig-cap: "Urban productivity indicators — NCR cities"
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-width: 10

p1 <- ggplot(ncr_city, aes(dist_cbd_km, mean_rentval)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "#c0392b",
              fill = "#fadbd8", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = "#2c3e50", size = 2.5) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = city), size = 2.8, max.overlaps = 15) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format(prefix = "₱")) +
  labs(title = "A. Rent Gradient",
       x = "Distance from CBD (km)", y = "Mean rent (PHP/yr)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

p2 <- ggplot(ncr_city, aes(dist_cbd_km, pct_college_grad)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "#2980b9",
              fill = "#d6eaf8", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = "#2c3e50", size = 2.5) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = city), size = 2.8, max.overlaps = 15) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(title = "B. Human Capital Gradient",
       x = "Distance from CBD (km)", y = "College grads (%)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

p3 <- ggplot(ncr_city, aes(pct_college_grad, mean_rentval)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "#16a085",
              fill = "#d1f2eb", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = "#2c3e50", size = 2.5) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = city), size = 2.8, max.overlaps = 15) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format(prefix = "₱")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(title = "C. Rent vs Human Capital",
       x = "College grads (%)", y = "Mean rent (PHP/yr)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

p4 <- ggplot(ncr_city, aes(wage_inc_share, mean_inc)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "#8e44ad",
              fill = "#e8daef", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = "#2c3e50", size = 2.5) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = city), size = 2.8, max.overlaps = 15) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma_format(prefix = "₱")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(title = "D. Wage Formality vs Income",
       x = "Wage share of income", y = "Mean income (PHP/yr)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

(p1 + p2) / (p3 + p4) +
  plot_annotation(
    title   = "Urban Productivity Dashboard — Metro Manila",
    subtitle = "FIES 2023 + CPH 2020 | City-level analysis (n = 17)",
    caption  = "Sources: PSA FIES 2023, CPH 2020",
    theme    = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13))
  )
```

## 6 · Exercises

::: callout-tip
**Exercise 1 — Map a new variable**\
Produce a choropleth map of `pct_makeshift_wall` (informality proxy).
Which cities have the highest rates? Does this align with what you know
about NCR urban geography?
:::

::: callout-tip
**Exercise 2 — Test a different gradient**\
Fit the log-linear gradient model using `pct_college_grad` as the
dependent variable instead of `mean_rentval`. Is the human capital
gradient steeper or flatter than the rent gradient?
:::

::: callout-tip
**Exercise 3 — OFW and rent**\
Plot `pct_ofw` (overseas workers) against `dist_cbd_km`. Do peripheral
cities have more OFWs? What might this tell us about the relationship
between local labour market opportunities and international migration?
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 7 · Key Takeaways

- **Spatial data in R** combines a geometry column with regular data
  frame columns, enabling seamless joins between tabular and geographic
  data
- The **land rent gradient** in Metro Manila broadly follows the AMM
  prediction: rent declines with distance from Makati CBD
- **Human capital** (college graduation) and **rent** are positively
  correlated across NCR cities, consistent with agglomeration theory
- **Anomalies** (San Juan's high rent, Valenzuela's high rent burden)
  are as instructive as the general pattern — they invite deeper
  investigation
